Shi'ur Qomah

Wheel of Heaven Translation

The Hekhalot/Merkavah mystical text describing the cosmic dimensions of the divine body — Siddur Rabbah recension. The 'Kabbalah' the Raëlian canon implicitly cites for *parasangs* measurements.

Direct Direct Established or uncontested across mainstream sources, or a direct description of the project itself. Framework Framework Foundational premise of the Wheel of Heaven framework. Explicit in the Raëlian canon; not endorsed by mainstream scholarship. Inferred Inferred A reasonable reading of comparative material — not stated literally, but consistent with the source. Speculative Speculative Interpretive synthesis or hypothesis that goes beyond what any single source states.

An English translation of the Shi'ur Qomah (Hebrew: שִׁעוּר קוֹמָה, 'The Measure of the Stature'), produced from a best-effort reconstruction based on named scholarly editions (verification pending against Cohen 1985 TSAJ 9). **The project's first Kabbalah / Jewish-mysticism-tradition text.** Chapter 1 covers the Siddur Rabbah recension — one of five recensions Cohen 1985 distinguishes (Sefer Hekhalot, Sefer Razim, Merkavah Rabbah, Siddur Rabbah, Ma'aseh Merkavah), and the most-cited 'standard' recension. Shi'ur Qomah is one of the oldest pieces of Jewish mystical literature (3rd–6th c. CE, with oral traditions reaching earlier — Scholem 1965 argues for tannaitic-era roots), preserved across Hekhalot literature. The text describes the cosmic measurements of the body of the Creator — the divine YOTZER — as a head-to-foot enumeration in which each limb is named with a secret magical name and measured in *parasangs* (Persian unit of distance adapted to cosmic scale: one parasang = 'as much as the entire universe is full'). The framing is a transmission from R. Yishmael (the famous high priest) to R. Akiva, then to the Hekhalot mystics. The implicit liturgical-theurgical function: knowing the names and measurements lets the mystic ascend the seven Hekhalot palaces and stand before the throne. **Reception is genuinely contested.** Maimonides (Iggeret Teiman; Mishneh Torah, Yesodei ha-Torah 1:8-12; Guide for the Perplexed I:35-36) condemned the text as un-Jewish and disputed its canonical status — calling it 'a forgery of a Greek preacher or a Karaite' (Iggeret Teiman). Conversely, R. Moses Cordovero, the Lurianic Kabbalists, and the Hasidic tradition treated it as authoritative. The text was central to the Hasidei Ashkenaz of medieval Germany and survived in Hekhalot anthologies through to the early-modern *Sefer Raziel ha-Mal'akh* printings. **Raëlian-canon engagement.** *The End of the World* and *At the Root of All Religions* both implicitly cite the Shi'ur Qomah tradition for its *parasangs* measurements and 'height of the creator' passages — making this translation a project priority for closing one of the genuine source-tensions named in the *Reference corpus of the Raëlian canon* wiki entry. The WoH-Translation pipeline produces the philologically-disciplined version, not the canon's pre-filtered version, with explicit operational disavowals against Sitchin/Anunnaki-engineered-deity-body and other lens-risk readings.

Chapter 1

Shi'ur Qomah, Siddur Rabbah recension — the cosmic measurements of the divine body and the magical names of its limbs

1
Shi'ur Qomah. Chapter 2.
שִׁעוּר Šiʿur קוֹמָה. Qōmâ. פ P[ereq] ב B[et]
Notes Verse 1

Structural heading: the manuscript-internal chapter division Perek Bet 'Chapter 2', the body-measurements core of the Siddur Rabbah recension. Cohen 1985 The Shi'ur Qomah: Texts and Recensions (TSAJ 9) reorganises this as approximately §§1-160 of his critical edition. The title Šiʿūr Qōmâ literally 'the measure of the stature' — preserved as untranslated title throughout the WoH-Translation per the central glossary entry.

2
R. Yishmael said: Metatron, the Great Prince of Testimony [Aramaic: śārāʾ rabbāʾ dĕ-šahădūṯāʾ], said to me: I testify with this testimony by YHWH, the Elohim of Israel, the living and enduring God, exalted and great, lofty and uplifted, who rescues us and redeems us and delivers me from every evil thing, and saves me from every kind of destroyer and from every kind of calamity. [Metatron's speech here is in Aramaic.]
אָמַר ʾāmar רַבִּי Rabbi יִשְׁמָעֵאל: Yišmāʿēʾl: אָמַר ʾāmar לִי lī מִיטַטְרוֹן Mīṭaṭrōn שָׂרָא śārāʾ רַבָּא rabbāʾ דְּשַׁהֲדוּתָא. dĕ-šahădūṯāʾ. מֵעִיד Mēʿīd אֲנִי ʾănī בְּעֵדוּת bĕ-ʿēdūṯ זוֹ zō בַּיהוה ba-YHWH אֱלֹהֵי ʾĕlōhē יִשְׂרָאֵל, Yiśrāʾēl, אֱלָהָא ʾĕlāhāʾ חַיָּא ḥayyāʾ וְקַיָּמָא, wĕ-qayyāmāʾ, מְרָנָנָא mĕrānĕnāʾ וְרַבְּבָנָא, wĕ-rabbĕbānāʾ, רַמְנָא ramnāʾ מְנַטְּלָא, mĕnaṭṭĕlāʾ, מְשֵׁזִיב mĕšēziḇ לָנָא lānāʾ וּמְפָרֵיק ū-mĕpāriq לָנָא lānāʾ וּמְפַלֵּט ū-mĕpalleṭ לִי lī מִכָּל mi-kol דְּבַר dĕḇar רַע, raʿ, וּמַצִּיל ū-maṣṣīl אוֹתִי ʾōtī מִכָּל mi-kol מִינֵי mīnē מַשְׁחִית mašḥīt וּמִכָּל ū-mi-kol מִינֵי mīnē פּוּרְעָנֻיּוֹת. pūrʿānuyyōt.
Notes Verse 2

Opening transmission-formula: R. Yishmael reports what Metatron told him. The Aramaic title שָׂרָא רַבָּא דְּשַׁהֲדוּתָא 'Great Prince of Testimony' is one of two Metatron-epithets in Shi'ur Qomah (the other being שַׂר הַפָּנִים 'Prince of the Presence/Face' at §8); the entire Metatron-speech is in Aramaic theurgical-mystical-prayer register (determinate-state -ā suffixes, the dĕ- relative, verb-forms like mĕšēziḇ 'rescuing'). Per the central glossary r-yishmael-r-akiva-hekhalot-transmission-chain-..., the R. Yishmael / R. Akiva tradent-frame is the Hekhalot literature's distinctive pseudo-tannaitic transmission-formula — the texts are 3rd-9th c. CE compositions claiming the authority of the 2nd c. CE tannaim. Lens-discipline disavowals applied: (i) no Christian-Christological pre-resolution of Metatron as pre-incarnate-Christ (the Hurtado 1988 / Boyarin 2012 / Schäfer 2012 scholarly dispute is preserved, not adjudicated); (ii) no Sitchin/Anunnaki engineered-emissary pre-resolution. Maimonides condemned this paragraph's framing in Iggeret Teiman as anthropomorphic-Christianising; the reception-dispute is genuine.

3
From the seat of his glory upward, 118 myriads, and from the seat of his glory downward, 118 myriads. His height is 236 myriads of thousands of parasangs. [Aramaic: 'the seat of his glory' and 'his height.']
שֶׁמִּבֵּית še-mi-bēt מוֹתַב mōtaḇ יְקָרֵיהּ yĕqārēh וּלְעֵלָּא ū-lĕ-ʿēllāʾ מֵאָה mēʾâ וּשְׁמוֹנֶה־עֶשְׂרֵה ū-šĕmōnâ-ʿeśrēh רִבְבוֹת, ribbĕḇōt, וּמִבֵּית ū-mi-bēt מוֹתַב mōtaḇ יְקָרֵיהּ yĕqārēh וּלְמַטָּה ū-lĕ-maṭṭâ מֵאָה mēʾâ וּשְׁמוֹנֶה־עֶשְׂרֵה ū-šĕmōnâ-ʿeśrēh רִבְבוֹת. ribbĕḇōt. רוּמֵיהּ Rūmēh מָאתַיִם māʾtayim וּשְׁלֹשִׁים ū-šĕlōšîm וְשִׁשָּׁה wĕ-šiššâ רִבְבוֹת ribbĕḇōt אֲלָפִים ʾălāp̄īm פַּרְסָאוֹת. parsāʾōt.
Notes Verse 3

The foundational 236-myriads cosmic measurement — the most-cited Shi'ur Qomah passage in scholarship (Cohen 1985 §§; Scholem 1965; Halperin 1988) and the highest-lens-risk site in the chapter. 118 myriads upward + 118 myriads downward = 236 myriads of thousands of parasangs of divine height. The gematria 236 is the numerical value of rûm 'height' as a hidden divine name (Scholem 1965); the structural symmetry (118 = 118) marks the cosmic-axis of the seat-of-glory.

MAJOR LENS-RISK DISAVOWAL — verbatim from the central entry. This translation does NOT support a Sitchin/Anunnaki/ancient-astronaut reading of the 236-myriads measurement as 'evidence of extraterrestrial body-dimensions of an engineered deity.' The cosmic-scale parasang is a theurgical-mystical-liturgical convention within the Hekhalot magical-name tradition (Cohen 1983 chs 3-5); its function is to mark the divine body as exceeding all human-scale measurement, not to provide actual measurements of any physical entity. The Raëlian canon's implicit citation of Shi'ur Qomah parasangs in The End of the World and At the Root of All Religions is acknowledged as a source-of-record reading that this entry does not endorse as the source-text's primary meaning. The internal definitional anchor at §31 — 'his span is the fullness of the whole world entire' — is the source-text's own apophatic disavowal of any literal-measurement reading.

Maimonides (Iggeret Teiman; Mishneh Torah, Yesodei ha-Torah 1:8-12) condemned this measurement-statement specifically as un-Jewish, calling it 'a forgery of a Greek preacher or a Karaite.' Cross-corpus: cf. 1 Enoch 14:18-22 (the throne-vision cosmic scale); Dan 7:9 (the Ancient of Days); Ezek 1:26-28 (the throne-figure).

4
From his right arm to his left arm, 77 myriads. From the socket of his right eye to the socket of his left eye, 30 myriads. The skull of his head [Aramaic], 333⅓. The crown on his head, 60 myriads, corresponding to the 60 myriads — the thousands of Israel.
מִזְּרוֹעוֹ mi-zĕrōʿō שֶׁל šel יָמִין yāmīn עַד ʿad זְרוֹעוֹ zĕrōʿō שֶׁל šel שְׂמֹאל śĕmōʾl שִׁבְעִים šiḇʿīm וְשֶׁבַע wā-šeḇaʿ רִבְבוֹת. ribbĕḇōt. מִגַּלְגַּל Mi-galgal עֵינָיו ʿēnāyw שֶׁל šel יָמִין yāmīn וְעַד wĕ-ʿad גַּלְגַּל galgal עֵינָיו ʿēnāyw שֶׁל šel שְׂמֹאל śĕmōʾl שְׁלֹשִׁים šĕlōšīm רִבְבוֹת. ribbĕḇōt. גֻּלְגֻּלְתָּא Gulguləttāʾ דְבְרֵאשֵׁיהּ ḏiḇ-rēšēh שְׁלֹשׁ šĕlōš מֵאוֹת mēʾōt וּשְׁלֹשִׁים ū-šĕlōšīm וּשְׁלוֹשׁ ū-šĕlōš וּשְׁלִישׁ. ū-šĕlīš. עֲטֶרֶת ʿăṭereṯ שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁוֹ še-bĕ-rōʾšō שִׁשִּׁים šiššīm רִבְבוֹת ribbĕḇōt כְּלַפֵּי kĕlappē שִׁשִּׁים šiššīm רִבְבוֹת ribbĕḇōt אַלְפֵי ʾalp̄ē יִשְׂרָאֵל. Yiśrāʾēl.
Notes Verse 4

Arm-to-arm 77 myriads; eye-socket-to-eye-socket 30 myriads. Skull-circumference 333⅓ (the cube of 11 / a gematric-significant fraction per Scholem 1965). Crown 60 myriads, explicitly correlated with the 600,000 Israelites at Sinai (Num 1:46; Exod 12:37): a structural pattern across Shi'ur Qomah in which divine measurements are sized against Israel's typological measurements. Halperin 1988 reads the correlation as evidence the body-measurement system is covenant-anchored, not pure speculation. The Aramaic determinate gulgultāʾ ḏiḇ-rēšēh 'the skull of his head' marks the theurgical-mystical register.

5
Therefore he is called the great, mighty, and awesome God: BLITEH YEDIDUT ELOHE BILTA BIZTA BEZUZTA HA-MQOQ HA-QATAF HA-QATAM QATAF — on account of joy. Blessed is the name of the glory of his kingdom forever and ever.
לְפִיכָךְ lĕ-p̄īḵāḵ נִקְרָא niqrāʾ הָאֵל hā-ʾēl הַגָּדוֹל ha-gādōl הַגִּבּוֹר ha-gibbōr וְהַנּוֹרָא wĕ-han-nōrāʾ בְּלִיתֵיהּ Bĕlîṯēh יְדִידוּת Yĕdīdūṯ אֱלֹהֵי ʾĔlōhē בִּילְתָּא Bīltāʾ בִּיזְתָא Bīzṯāʾ בְּזוּזְתָא Bĕzūztāʾ הַמְקוֹק Ha-Mqōq הַקָּטָף Ha-Qāṭāp̄ הַקָּטָם Ha-Qāṭām קָטָף Qāṭāp̄ בַּעֲבוּר baʿăḇūr מָשׂוֹשׂ. māśōś. בָּרוּךְ Bārūḵ שֵׁם šēm כְּבוֹד kĕḇōd מַלְכוּתוֹ malkūtō לְעוֹלָם lĕ-ʿōlām וָעֶד. wā-ʿed.
Notes Verse 5

String of magical-name divine-epithets (Jellinek 1853 PD; Cohen 1985 collates variants 'BLYTH', 'BZWZTA', 'HMQQ' across the Schäfer 1981 Synopse witnesses). The canonical liturgical epithet הָאֵל הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא 'the great, mighty, and awesome God' is from Deut 10:17. The closing בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם doxology serves a theurgical-protective function for the reciter who has just heard a string of secret names.

6
And whoever knows this mystery is assured of the life of the world to come, and is rescued from the judgment of Gehinnom, and is rescued from all harsh decrees, and is rescued from every kind of sorcery and from every kind of calamity.
וְכָל wĕ-ḵol הַיּוֹדֵעַ hay-yōdēaʿ רָז rāz זֶה zeh מֻבְטָח muḇṭāḥ לוֹ lō לְחַיֵּי lĕ-ḥayyē הָעוֹלָם hā-ʿōlām הַבָּא, hab-bāʾ, וְנִצּוֹל wĕ-niṣṣōl מִדִּינָהּ mid-dīnâ שֶׁל šel גֵּיהִנֹּם, gēhinnōm, וְנִצּוֹל wĕ-niṣṣōl מִכָּל mi-kol גְּזֵרוֹת gĕzērōt קָשׁוֹת, qāšōt, וְנִצּוֹל wĕ-niṣṣōl מִכָּל mi-kol מִינֵי mīnē כְשָׁפִים kĕšāp̄īm וּמִכָּל ū-mi-kol מִינֵי mīnē פּוּרְעָנֻיּוֹת. pūrʿānuyyōt.
Notes Verse 6

The theurgical-reward formula in its early form (reiterated more fully at §§40-41 with the explicit Yishmael+Akiva guarantor-statement). 'Whoever knows this rāz (mystery)' inherits the world-to-come and gains protection from Gehenna, harsh decrees, and sorceries. Maimonides condemned this principle (Mishneh Torah, Yesodei ha-Torah 1:8-12) as un-Jewish theurgy: the m. Sanhedrin 10:1 baseline (kol Yiśrāʾēl yēš lāhem ḥēleq lā-ʿôlām hab-bāʾ 'all Israel have a share in the world-to-come') is here recast around esoteric-knowledge possession. Scholem 1965 reads this in the technical sense of gnōsis (saving knowledge); Halperin 1988, Schäfer 1992, and Boustan 2005 contest the gnostic label. The reception-dispute is preserved, not adjudicated.

7
R. Yishmael said: I saw the King of the kings of kings, blessed be He, seated upon a throne high and lifted up, and his armies standing before him on his right and on his left.
אָמַר ʾāmar רַבִּי Rabbi יִשְׁמָעֵאל: Yišmāʿēʾl: אֲנִי ʾănī רָאִיתִי rāʾītī אֶת ʾeṯ מֶלֶךְ meleḵ מַלְכֵי malḵē הַמְּלָכִים ham-mĕlāḵīm בָּרוּךְ bārūḵ הוּא hūʾ שֶׁהוּא še-hūʾ יוֹשֵׁב yōšēḇ עַל ʿal כִּסֵּא kissēʾ רָם rām וְנִשָּׂא, wĕ-niśśāʾ, וְחֵילוֹתָיו wĕ-ḥēlōtāyw עוֹמְדִים ʿōmĕdīm לְפָנָיו lĕ-p̄ānāyw מִימִינוֹ mīmīnō וּמִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ. ū-mi-śśĕmōʾlō.
Notes Verse 7

The throne-vision opening — direct allusion to Isa 6:1 (Isaiah's call-vision: 'I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up') reworked as Hekhalot first-person ascent-vision. Cross-corpus: 1 Kgs 22:19 (Micaiah's throne-vision with hosts to right and left); Dan 7:9-10; Ezek 1:26-28; Rev 4:2-6. The phrase מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים 'King of kings of kings' is the standard Hekhalot intensification (cf. b. Berakhot 28b and throughout Hekhalot Rabbati). The first-person 'I saw' is the visionary-experience claim Maimonides specifically rejected (Mishneh Torah, Yesodei ha-Torah 1:9: no human eye has seen the divine form). Lens-discipline disavowal: no Sitchin-merkavah-as-spaceship pre-resolution (Blumrich 1974 Spaceships of Ezekiel is a 20th-c. interpretive overlay this translation does not endorse).

8
The angel, the Prince of the Presence, whose name is Metatron RUAḤ PISQONYAH PISQON ITIMON HIGRON ⟨…⟩ QAM ḤIQRON ZIWA RABBA NANṬAM ZANṬOF, said to me: [the illegible portion is preserved from the source].
אָמַר ʾāmar לִי lī מַלְאָךְ malʾāḵ שַׂר śar הַפָּנִים hap-pānīm שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ še-šĕmō מִיטַטְרוֹן Mīṭaṭrōn רוּחַ Rūaḥ פִּסְקוֹנְיָה Pisqōnyâ פִּסְקוֹן Pisqōn אִיטִימוֹן ʾĪṭīmōn הִיגְרוֹן Hīgrōn ‹...› ‹...› קָם Qām חִיקְרוֹן Ḥīqrōn זִיוָא Zīwāʾ רַבָּא Rabbāʾ נַנְטָם Nanṭām זַנְטוֹף. Zanṭōp̄.
Notes Verse 8

Metatron's secret-name list (~14 distinct names: PISQONYAH, PISQON, ITIMON, HIGRON, QAM, ḤIQRON, ZIWA RABBA, NANṬAM, ZANṬOF). The names vary across manuscripts (Cohen 1985 / Schäfer 1981 Synopse read 'PSQWNYH PSQWN AYTYMWN' as the stable core, with variants in HIGRON/YYGRWN and NNTAM/NNTYM). Cross-corpus to 3 Enoch ch 48D ('70 names of Metatron') and the broader Hekhalot many-named-Metatron tradition. The lacuna ⟨…⟩ is preserved from the source manuscript-witnesses where the consonants are illegible.

9
R. Yishmael says: how great is the measure of the stature of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is concealed from all creatures.
רַבִּי Rabbi יִשְׁמָעֵאל Yišmāʿēʾl אוֹמֵר: ʾōmēr: כַּמָּה kammâ שִׁעוּר šiʿūr קוֹמָתוֹ qōmātō שֶׁל šel הַקָּדוֹשׁ hak-qādōš בָּרוּךְ bārūḵ הוּא hūʾ שֶׁהוּא še-hūʾ מְכֻסֶּה mĕḵusseh מִכָּל mi-kol הַבְּרִיּוֹת. hab-bĕriyyōt.
Notes Verse 9

The formula-question that introduces the body-measurement enumeration proper. 'How great is the measure of the stature of the Holy One, Blessed be He, who is concealed from all creatures?' — the paradox-formula (hidden, yet measurable) is the central interpretive crux. Halperin 1988 / Cohen 1983 / Scholem 1965 all read this paradox as the key against literal-anthropomorphic readings: the divine is mĕḵusseh mi-kol hab-bĕriyyôt 'concealed from all creatures' precisely in the moment of being measured. Maimonides took the formula at face value as literal-anthropomorphism (and rejected the entire project on that basis); Cordovero, Luria, and the Hasidei Ashkenaz read the formula as symbolic-theosophical exposition. Lens-discipline disavowal: the cosmic-body-measurement is NOT engineered-deity-body in the Sitchin / ancient-astronaut sense.

10
The soles of his feet fill the whole world entire, as it is said: 'Thus said YHWH: the skies are my throne and the land is my footstool' [Isa 66:1]. The height of his soles ⟨…⟩ 6,000 parasangs.

Notes Verse 10

The head-to-foot body-measurement begins. The soles of his feet 'fill the whole world entire', the scriptural anchor Isa 66:1 ('the skies are my throne and the land is my footstool') providing the prooftext. Cohen 1985 notes the recursive structure: §§11-29 enumerate feet-to-neck upward, then §§22-38 return head-downward. Comparative-mythology cross-reference: the cosmic-body-whose-feet-rest-on-the-earth pattern parallels the Vedic Puruṣa-sūkta (RV 10.90) — see central entry purusha-sukta-.... Explicit comparative-typological-only flag: the parallel is comparative-mythological-typological, NOT genetic-cognate; Indo-Aryan vs Semitic, no transmission-channel.

Begin per-limb bilateral-symmetry enumeration. Right/left/right/left pattern continues through §§29; each measurement preserved exactly. Notes Verse 16

Major magical-name passage: 'seventy names' inscribed on the divine heart. The text actually contains far more than seventy distinct strings; the 'seventy' is typological, not literal (Scholem 1965). Canonical divine epithets are interwoven with magical-name strings: Ṣedeq, Ṣur, Ṣaddiq, Ṣevaot, Shadday, Elohim, YHWH alongside consonantal-cluster names (PPP, NN, HH, etc.). The scriptural anchor Ps 68:5 (חַי...רוֹכֵב עֲרָבוֹת 'Living one, Rider on the clouds') ties the magical-name list to the liturgical Berakhot. Cross-corpus: cf. Rev 19:12 (the rider-on-white-horse 'has a name written that no one knows but himself'). Lens-discipline disavowal: the secret-name-on-the-heart concept is the Hekhalot magical-theurgical convention (Cohen 1983 chs 3-5); no Sitchin/Anunnaki engineered-deity-implant reading.

Notes Verse 18

Head-circumference 3,000,000 myriads + 33⅓ — amplifying the §4 gematric pattern. The ineffability-formula 'that which the mouth cannot speak and the ear cannot hear' is the rabbinic-mystic ineffability topos with direct intertexts at Isa 64:3 and 1 Cor 2:9. Cross-corpus: Hekhalot Rabbati §§94-105 throne-vision ineffability passages; 2 Cor 12:2-4 (Paul's 'third heaven' ineffability). Lens-discipline disavowal: no Christian-Apocalyptic pre-resolution of the Pauline parallel (the shared substrate is real; the Christian-eschatological development is downstream).

19
His beard, a myriad and 1,500 parasangs. Its name is HADRAQMASYA. And the appearance of the face and the appearance of the cheeks is like the form of a breath and in the shape of a soul; no creature is able to recognize it.
זְקָנוֹ zĕqānō רִבּוֹ ribbō וְאֶלֶף wĕ-ʾelep̄ וַחֲמֵשׁ wa-ḥămēš מֵאוֹת mēʾōt פַּרְסָאוֹת. parsāʾōt. הַדְרַקְמַסְיָא HaDraqmasyāʾ שְׁמוֹ. šĕmō. וּמַרְאֵה Ū-marʾēh הַפָּנִים hap-pānīm וּמַרְאֵה ū-marʾēh הַלְּסָתוֹת hal-lĕsāṯōt כִּדְמוּת ki-dĕmūṯ רוּחַ rūaḥ וּבְצוּרַת ū-bĕ-ṣūrat נְשָׁמָה, nĕšāmâ, אֵין ʾēn כָּל kol בְּרִיָּה bĕriyyâ יְכוֹלָה yĕḵōlâ לְהַכִּירוֹ. lĕ-hakkīrō.
Notes Verse 19

The anti-anthropomorphic kernel: 'the appearance of the face and cheeks is like the form of a breath [rûaḥ] and in the shape of a soul [nĕšāmâ]; no creature is able to recognize it.' The face is unrecognisable even as it is named and measured — the apophatic-anthropomorphic paradox at maximum intensity. Cohen 1983 ch 4 / Scholem 1965 / Halperin 1988 all treat this passage as the central interpretive lever against literal-anthropomorphic readings. Cross-corpus: Exod 33:20-23 (Moses sees only the 'back'); Dan 7:9 (the Ancient of Days' face); Rev 1:14-16 (the white-haired one's face like the sun). The translation of rûaḥ as 'breath' is consistent with the production glossary ruach-elohim convention (Gen 1:2).

20
His body is like tarshish-stone. His radiance is distinct, awesome, out of the darkness. Cloud and thick darkness surround him. All the princes of the ofannim are poured out before him like a flagon. גְּוִיָּתוֹ gĕwîyāṯō כְּתַרְשִׁישׁ. kĕ-Taršīš. זִיווֹ Zīwō מֻבְהָק muḇhāq נוֹרָא nōrāʾ מִתּוֹךְ mit-tōḵ הַחֹשֶׁךְ. ha-ḥōšeḵ. וְעָנָן Wĕ-ʿānān וַעֲרָפֶל wa-ʿărāp̄el מַקִּיפִין maqqīp̄īn אוֹתוֹ. ʾōtō. וְכָל Wĕ-ḵol שָׂרֵי śārē הָאוֹפַנִּים hā-ʾōp̄annīm נִשְׁפָּכִים nišpāḵīm לְפָנָיו lĕ-p̄ānāyw כְּקִיתוֹן. kĕ-qītōn. אֵין ʾēn בְּיָדֵינוּ bĕ-yādēnū מִדָּה middâ אֶלָּא ʾellāʾ שֵׁמוֹת šēmōt מְגוּלִּין mĕgūllīn לָנוּ: lānū: הַחוֹשָׁם Ha-Ḥōšām פַּגְבַּגְצִיָּא Pagbagṣîyâʾ שְׁמוֹ, šĕmō, אַבְרַגַּגְטַפִיָּא ʾAḇragagṭap̄îyâʾ שְׁמוֹ. šĕmō.
Notes Verse 20

Body 'like tarshish-stone' — direct citation of Cant 5:14 (gĕlîlê zāhāḇ mĕmullāʾîm bĕ-Tarshîš 'rods of gold set with tarshish-stone'); cross-reference to Dan 10:6 (the divine messenger 'his body was like tarshish'). 'Cloud and thick darkness surround him' echoes Ps 97:2 / Exod 19:9. Apophatic methodological admission: 'we have no measure, only names revealed to us' — Halperin 1988 cites this as the key text against literal-anthropomorphic readings: the magical-name system substitutes for any actual quantitative measurement at this site. The ofannim are the wheels of Ezek 1:15-21.

21
His tongue reaches from one end of the world to its other end, as it is said: 'He declares his words to Jacob' [Ps 147:19]. Whoever does not seal with this verse errs: 'He declares his words to Jacob, his statutes and his judgments to Israel.' Its name is ASASGIHUWAYA.
לְשׁוֹנוֹ lĕšōnō מִסּוֹף mis-sōp̄ הָעוֹלָם hā-ʿōlām וְעַד wĕ-ʿad סוֹפוֹ. sōp̄ō. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: Šen-neʾĕmar: «מַגִּיד 'Maggīd דְּבָרָיו dĕḇārāyw לְיַעֲקֹב». lĕ-Yaʿăqōḇ.' כָּל Kol שֶׁאֵינוֹ še-ʾēnō חוֹתֵם ḥōtēm בַּפָּסוּק bap-pāsūq הַזֶּה haz-zeh הֲרֵי hărē זֶה zeh שׁוֹגֶה: šōgeh: «מַגִּיד 'Maggīd דְּבָרָיו dĕḇārāyw לְיַעֲקֹב lĕ-Yaʿăqōḇ חֻקָּיו ḥuqqāyw וּמִשְׁפָּטָיו ū-mišpāṭāyw לְיִשְׂרָאֵל». lĕ-Yiśrāʾēl.' אַסַסְגִּיהוּוָאיָא ʾAsasgīhūwāʾyāʾ שְׁמוֹ. šĕmō.
Notes Verse 21

Tongue 'from the end of the world to its other end' (uncountable / cosmic-spanning). Scriptural prooftext Ps 147:19 is supplied with a verse-sealing instruction: 'whoever does not seal with this verse errs' — the recurring theurgical-recitation rule. Schäfer 1992 reads this as evidence of Shi'ur Qomah being a recitation-protocol (not a doctrinal exposition): the prooftexts must be cited in full to retain protective efficacy. Cross-corpus: m. Megillah 4:10 (the prooftext-completion principle in synagogue Torah-reading).

Notes Verse 22

Major magical-name passage: the 72-letter Name (Shem ben-AB) is one of the most-studied features of Jewish mysticism, derived from the three-verse Exod 14:19-21 sequence (each verse exactly 72 letters). Cross-corpus: Ezek 9:4 (the mark on the foreheads of those who lament); the high-priestly ṣîṣ with 'Holiness to YHWH' (Exod 28:36-38); the tefillin tradition (Deut 6:8); Rev 7:3, 14:1, 22:4 (the seal/name on the foreheads of the 144,000). Multiple lens-discipline disavowals applied (see central entry seal-on-forehead-...): (i) no Sitchin/ancient-astronaut 'implant on forehead' reading; (ii) no Christian-Apocalyptic mark-of-the-beast typology pre-resolution; (iii) no popular-fringe gnostic-techno-sealing reading.

The angelic-prince-per-limb pattern activates: the right pupil is governed by RAḤAVIEL (one of the named Hekhalot angelic princes). Notes Verse 31

The definitional-anchor passage — crucial disavowal anchor for the entire chapter. Metatron provides the internal definition: parasang = 3 miles; mile = 10,000 cubits; cubit = ⟨...⟩ spans by his span; and his span is the fullness of the whole world entire. The scriptural prooftext Isa 40:12 supplies the apophatic frame: the divine span is by definition cosmic-scale. The chain makes the §3 measurement system internally consistent and explicitly NOT a literal physical-body measurement: each parasang is itself cosmic-scale, so 236 myriads of thousands of cosmic-parasangs is by definition not addable into a finite physical dimension. Maimonides (Iggeret Teiman) read this passage as proof the body-measurements are at most allegorical; Cohen 1983 ch 5 reads it as the apophatic anchor. Lens-discipline disavowal: the Raëlian-canon implicit parasangs citation flows through the §3 measurement; the §31 definitional passage is the source-text's own apophatic guard against any literal-physical-dimensional reading.

32
R. Nathan, disciple of R. Yishmael, says: he also gave me the measure of the nose, measure by measure assured; and likewise the lip, and likewise the cheeks. Even though he gave me the measure of the forehead, he also gave me the measure of the cubit ⟨of the side⟩: of the loin. The breadth of the forehead is as the height of the neck; likewise the shoulder is as the length of the nose; the length of the nose is as the length of the little finger.

R. Nathan enters as a second tradent (disciple of R. Yishmael); Cohen 1985 reads this as evidence the Siddur Rabbah recension integrates a parallel transmission-chain. R. Halperin 1988 reads this as the iconographic (vs gigantic) interpretive register: the proportional ratios for the divine body are the same proportional ratios as the human body, differing only in scale — anticipating the imago-dei claim at §33.

Notes Verse 34

Major lens-risk + Maimonidean-condemnation site. (a) The divine crown is named ISRAEL — the people-of-Israel as the divine crown-name (the covenantal-anchoring of the Shi'ur Qomah project). (b) The non-biblical 'Israel my people, mine' inscription between the horns. (c) The Cant 5:10-13 citation: the bride's wāṣf-of-the-bridegroom read as a literal description of the divine body — Halperin 1988 argues Cant 5:10-16 is the source-text Shi'ur Qomah is exegeting (see central entry cant-5-10-16-...). R. Akiva endorsed the Cant-as-Holy-of-Holies reading (m. Yadayim 3:5); Maimonides condemned exactly this allegorical-reading-strategy in Iggeret Teiman as the smoking-gun of Shi'ur Qomah's un-Jewishness. (d) 'Horns' (qarnāyw) — Maimonides read literal; Hasidei Ashkenaz read as 'rays of light' (cf. Hab 3:4). The translation preserves all literal; the reception-dispute is not adjudicated.

It turns out that the whole measure entire is a great-many-myriads of myriads of thousands of parasangs in height, and a thousand thousand myriads of parasangs in breadth.
נִמְצָא Nimṣāʾ כָּל kol הַשִּׁעוּר haš-šiʿūr כֻּלּוֹ kullō רֹב rōḇ רִבֵּי ribbē רִבְבוֹת ribbĕḇōt אֲלָפִים ʾălāp̄īm פַּרְסָאוֹת parsāʾōt גֹּבַהּ. gōḇah. וְאֶלֶף Wĕ-ʾelep̄ אֲלָפִים ʾălāp̄īm רִבְבוֹת ribbĕḇōt פַּרְסִיּוֹת parsīyōt רֹחַב. rōḥaḇ.
Notes Verse 39

Summary recapitulation. Maimonides specifically rejected the addability of the chapter's numbers as evidence the text could not be allegorical (if the individual measurements summed to a coherent total, the whole was either literal or absurd); Cohen 1983 / Halperin 1988 read the unstable summary-total here ('a great-many-myriads of myriads') as evidence the numbers are typological-symbolic, not arithmetic-summable. The summary preserves the symbolic-incommensurable register.

Notes Verse 40

The R. Yishmael → R. Akiva chain-of-transmission confirmation. The YOTZER (Creator) epithet appears explicitly — Shi'ur Qomah identifies the body being measured with YOTZER, the Creator, not with a hypostatic intermediary (no 'lesser YHWH' / Logos / Sophia / Demiurge intermediary between the unknowable divine and the cosmos). This is the text's distinctive theological commitment (see central entry yotzer-bereshit-...). The transliteration yotzer is bracketed-preserved to flag the technical theological term.

41
R. Yishmael said: I and R. Akiva are guarantors in this matter — that whoever knows this measure of our Creator [yotzer] and the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, is assured that he is a child of the world to come; provided only that he recites it as Mishnah every single day.
אָמַר ʾāmar רַבִּי Rabbi יִשְׁמָעֵאל: Yišmāʿēʾl: אֲנִי ʾănī וְרַבִּי wĕ-Rabbi עֲקִיבָא ʿĂqīḇāʾ עֲרֵבִים ʿărēḇīm בַּדָּבָר bad-dāḇār זֶה, zeh, שֶׁכָּל še-ḵol מִי mī שֶׁהוּא še-hūʾ יוֹדֵעַ yōdēaʿ שִׁעוּר šiʿūr הַזֶּה haz-zeh שֶׁל šel יוֹצְרֵנוּ yōṣĕrēnū וְשִׁבְחוֹ wĕ-šiḇḥō שֶׁל šel הַקָּדוֹשׁ־בָּרוּךְ־הוּא, hak-qādōš-bārūḵ-hūʾ, מֻבְטָח muḇṭāḥ לוֹ lō שֶׁהוּא še-hūʾ בֶּן ben הָעוֹלָם hā-ʿōlām הַבָּא. hab-bāʾ. וּבִלְבַד Ū-ḇi-lḇaḏ שֶׁהוּא še-hūʾ שׁוֹנֶה šōneh אוֹתוֹ ʾōtō בַּמִּשְׁנָה bam-mišnâ בְּכָל bĕ-ḵol יוֹם yōm וָיוֹם. wā-yōm.
Notes Verse 41

The most-cited Shi'ur Qomah passage in rabbinic-liturgical reception: the famous Yishmael+Akiva guarantor-formula. The two tannaim pledge themselves as ʿărēḇîm (sureties — in the technical m. Bava Batra 10:7 surety-law sense) for the outcome that whoever recites the body-measurement as Mishnah every day inherits the world-to-come. Cohen 1983 ch 6 reads this as the structural-functional key to the entire Shi'ur Qomah text: the chapter is a theurgical-praxis manual in the form of a body-measurement enumeration. Maimonides condemned this formula specifically in Iggeret Teiman as 'absurd, contrary to all Torah' — the principle that esoteric-knowledge possession could substitute for the standard m. Sanhedrin 10:1 conditions for the world-to-come was the smoking-gun of Shi'ur Qomah's un-Jewishness on the Maimonidean view. Lens-discipline disavowal: the 'eternal-life-via-esoteric-knowledge' here is the Hekhalot-theurgical-Mishnah-recitation discipline; NO Raëlian-canon cellular-cloning-eternal-life pre-resolution; NO Christian-salvific-knowledge (gnostic gnōsis-as-salvation) pre-resolution. The Maimonidean-vs-mystical reception-dispute is preserved, not adjudicated.

Mīṭaṭrōn. אוֹמְרֵי ʾŌmĕrē עִזּוּז ʿizzūz וְגִבּוֹר wĕ-gibbōr וְאוֹמְרֵי wĕ-ʾōmĕrē «קָדוֹשׁ» 'qādōš' וּבָרוּךְ ū-ḇārūḵ הוּא hūʾ וְאוֹמְרֵי wĕ-ʾōmĕrē הֲמֻלָּה hămullâ בָּאִין bāʾīn וְעוֹמְדִין wĕ-ʿōmĕḏīn לִפְנֵי lip̄nē הַנַּעַר. han-naʿar.
Notes Verse 52

Major Christological-typology lens-risk site — Metatron as 'the youth' (han-naʿar) receiving the divine hand on his head as coronation/empowerment. Cross-corpus: Dan 7:13 bar ʾĕnāš 'son of man'; 1 Enoch 71 (Enoch-as-Son-of-Man); b. Hagigah 15a (Metatron-and-Aher controversy with explicit naʿar identification); b. Sanhedrin 38b two-powers polemic; Isa 9:5 'child given.' Lens-discipline disavowals: (i) no Christian-Christological pre-resolution of Metatron as pre-incarnate-Christ; the Boyarin 2012-vs-Schäfer 2012 scholarly dispute is preserved, not adjudicated; (ii) no Sitchin/Anunnaki 'young intermediary' pre-resolution; (iii) no Jungian/New-Age 'archetype of the divine child' pre-resolution. The Hekhalot Metatron-the-youth is a theological-mystical-angelological figure inside the late-antique Jewish synagogue/study-house cultural setting.

53
And the youth comes and prostrates himself before the Holy One, blessed be He — his name AHAH and praised — and says: 'Blessed is the glory of YHWH from his place' [Ezek 3:12]. YEHU HOHU YOHI YAH YEHI. And they say after him: Blessed is the name of the glory of his kingdom forever and ever.

Yĕhī. וְהֵן Wĕ-hen אוֹמְרִין ʾōmĕrīn אַחֲרָיו: ʾaḥărāyw: בָּרוּךְ bārūḵ שֵׁם šēm כְּבוֹד kĕḇōd מַלְכוּתוֹ malḵūtō לְעוֹלָם lĕ-ʿōlām וָעֶד. wā-ʿed.
Notes Verse 53

Metatron-the-youth prostrates before the Holy One — explicitly servant-posture, not co-equal. The scriptural anchor Ezek 3:12 ('Blessed is the glory of YHWH from his place') is the canonical Qedushah de-Sidra liturgical formula.

54
And he enters beneath the throne of glory. And when he is ⟨…⟩ beneath the throne of glory, at his right walk LIVARNE of fire, and stones of hail, and walls of wrath. And at his left walk wings of tempest and mighty acts of storm.
וְנִכְנָס Wĕ-niḵnās לְתַחַת lĕ-taḥaṯ כִּסֵּא kissēʾ הַכָּבוֹד. hak-kāḇōḏ. וּכְשֶׁהוּא Ū-ḵe-še-hūʾ ‹...› ‹...› תַּחַת taḥaṯ כִּסֵּא kissēʾ הַכָּבוֹד hak-kāḇōḏ מְהַלְּכִין mĕhalĕḵīn לִימִינוֹ lī-mīnō לִיבָרְנֵי līḇārĕnē שֶׁל šel אֵשׁ ʾēš וַאֲבָנִים wa-ʾăḇānīm שֶׁל šel בָּרָד bārād וְכָתֳלִים wĕ-ḵātŏlīm שֶׁל šel זַעַף. zaʿap̄. וּלְרוּחַ Ū-lĕ-rūaḥ שְׂמֹאלוֹ śĕmōʾlō מְהַלְּכִין mĕhalĕḵīn כַּנְפוֹת kanp̄ōt סְעָרָה sĕʿārâ וּגְבוּרוֹת ū-ḡĕḇūrōt שֶׁל šel סוּפָה. sūp̄â.
Notes Verse 54

Metatron-the-youth's entry beneath the throne — the cosmic-servant station distinct from the throne-itself. The 'stones of hail' echoes Job 38:22 / Ezek 38:22.

55
And when the youth enters beneath the throne of glory, the Holy One, blessed be He, strengthens him with abundance of presence. And they praise the Holy One, blessed be He, three times every single day by means of the youth.

The ministering angels praise the Holy One by means of (ʿal yĕdê) the youth — Metatron-the-youth as the liturgical-mediating figure, with the Deut 10:17 'great, mighty, and awesome God' epithet repeated.

56
And the Holy One, blessed be He, bestows of his radiance and of his majesty upon the kings of the nations of the world. And this youth — his stature fills the world, and the Holy One, blessed be He, calls him 'youth.' And this youth is Metatron, Prince of the Presence, who is inscribed as the Great Prince over all the princes and over all the ministering angels ⟨…⟩ they stand before him, and he stands above on high and ministers before a consuming fire. His name is DASSA.
וְנוֹתֵן Wĕ-nōtēn הַקָּדוֹשׁ־בָּרוּךְ־הוּא hak-qādōš-bārūḵ-hūʾ מִזִּיווֹ mi-zīwō וּמֵהֲדָרוֹ ū-mē-hădārō עַל ʿal מַלְכֵי malḵē אֻמּוֹת ʾumōt הָעוֹלָם. hā-ʿōlām. וְהַנַּעַר Wĕ-han-naʿar הַזֶּה haz-zeh קוֹמָתוֹ qōmātō מְלֹא mĕlōʾ הָעוֹלָם hā-ʿōlām וְקוֹרֵא wĕ-qōrēʾ אוֹתוֹ ʾōtō הַקָּדוֹשׁ־בָּרוּךְ־הוּא hak-qādōš-bārūḵ-hūʾ נַעַר. naʿar. וְהַנַּעַר Wĕ-han-naʿar זֶה zeh זֶה zeh מִיטַטְרוֹן Mīṭaṭrōn שַׂר śar הַפָּנִים hap-pānīm שֶׁנִּכְתָּב šen-niḵtāḇ שַׂר śar הַגָּדוֹל hag-gādōl עַל ʿal כָּל kol הַשָּׂרִים haś-śārīm וְעַל wĕ-ʿal כָּל kol מַלְאֲכֵי malʾăḵē הַשָּׁרֵת haš-šārēt ‹...› ‹...› עוֹמְדִין ʿōmĕḏīn לְפָנָיו lip̄nāyw וְהוּא wĕ-hūʾ עוֹמֵד ʿōmēḏ לְמַעְלָה lĕ-maʿlâ לַמָּרוֹם lam-mārōm וּמְשַׁמֵּשׁ ū-mĕšammēš לִפְנֵי lip̄nē אֵשׁ ʾēš אוֹכֵלָה. ʾōḵēlâ. דַּסָּא Dassâ שְׁמוֹ. šĕmō.
Notes Verse 56

Lens-risk site — Metatron's cosmic stature 'fills the world.' Metatron-the-youth has the cosmic-dimensional property of §3 BUT as servant: the Holy One calls him naʿar. The Hekhalot tradition is clear: Metatron is the cosmic-servant, not the Creator (the body measured at §3 is YOTZER per §§40-41); the cosmic-dimensional property attaches to Metatron's servant-role, not to a Creator-status. Lens-discipline disavowals: (i) no Sitchin/Anunnaki engineered-deity-body conflation (Metatron-the-cosmic-servant is a theological-mystical-angelological figure, not an embodied 'designer-emissary'); (ii) no Christian-Trinitarian / Logos pre-resolution of the cosmic-Metatron as a co-equal divine person.

57
This is Metatron, Prince of the Presence, who is inscribed in one letter by which the skies and the land were shaped and which was sealed with the signet 'Ehyeh asher Ehyeh' [Exod 3:14], and inscribed in six letters, and in seven letters, and in twenty-two letters; and in seventy names, and in seven sanctifications. And he was given by six of their names. And he was engraved upon twelve stones. And he was inscribed in seven voices, in six over the height of six, and given in chambers of chambers and in secrets of secrets and in wonders of wonders to Moses.

Notes Verse 57

Metatron's letter-cosmology: inscribed in one letter by which the skies and the land were shaped (anticipating Sefer Yetzirah's letter-cosmogony); sealed with the signet ʾEhyeh ʾăšer ʾEhyeh (Exod 3:14 burning-bush self-naming); inscribed in 6, 7, 22, 70 names; the Mosaic-transmission claim ('to Moses, in chambers of chambers, secrets of secrets, wonders of wonders'). Cross-corpus: b. Shabbat 88b (Moses receiving secrets in heaven); b. Sanhedrin 38b. The numerological-letter scheme is pre-Sefirotic qabalistic-numerological pattern.

58
And the Holy One, blessed be He, did not grant permission to make use of him — neither to the first human, nor to Shem the Great, nor to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob — but only to Moses, as it is said: 'Behold, I am sending an angel before you' [Exod 23:20]. And the Holy One, blessed be He, warned Moses to be on guard with him, as it is said: 'Be on your guard before him and listen to his voice; do not rebel against him' [Exod 23:21]. And Moses said before the Holy One, blessed be He: 'If your presence does not go, do not bring us up from here' [Exod 33:15].
וְלֹא Wĕ-lōʾ נָתַן nāṯan הַקָּדוֹשׁ־בָּרוּךְ־הוּא hak-qādōš-bārūḵ-hūʾ רְשׁוּת rĕšūt לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ lĕ-hištammēš בּוֹ bō וְלֹא wĕ-lōʾ לְאָדָם lĕ-ʾāḏām הָרִאשׁוֹן hā-riʾšōn וְלֹא wĕ-lōʾ לְשֵׁם lĕ-Šēm הַגָּדוֹל hag-gādōl וְלֹא wĕ-lōʾ לְאַבְרָהָם lĕ-ʾAḇrāhām לְיִצְחָק lĕ-Yiṣḥāq וּלְיַעֲקֹב ū-lĕ-Yaʿăqōḇ אֶלָּא ʾellāʾ לְמֹשֶׁה lĕ-Mōšeh בִּלְבַד. bi-lḇaḏ. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: Šen-neʾĕmar: «הִנֵּה 'hinnēh אָנֹכִי ʾānōḵī שׁוֹלֵחַ šōlēaḥ מַלְאָךְ malʾāḵ לְפָנֶיךָ». lĕ-p̄āneḵā.' וְהִזְהִיר Wĕ-hizhīr הַקָּדוֹשׁ־בָּרוּךְ־הוּא hak-qādōš-bārūḵ-hūʾ אֶת ʾeṯ מֹשֶׁה Mōšeh שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּמֵּר še-yištammēr בּוֹ, bō, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: šen-neʾĕmar: «הִשָּׁמֶר 'hiššāmer מִפָּנָיו mip-pānāyw וּשְׁמַע ū-šĕmaʿ בְּקֹלוֹ bĕ-qōlō אַל ʾal תַּמֵּר tammēr בּוֹ». bō.' וּמֹשֶׁה Ū-Mōšeh אָמַר ʾāmar לִפְנֵי lip̄nē הַקָּדוֹשׁ־בָּרוּךְ־הוּא: hak-qādōš-bārūḵ-hūʾ: «אִם 'ʾim אֵין ʾēn פָּנֶיךָ pāneḵā הוֹלְכִים hōlĕḵīm אַל ʾal תַּעֲלֵנוּ taʿălēnū מִזֶּה». miz-zeh.'
Notes Verse 58

The classical Hekhalot Metatron-as-Exodus-angel reading, identifying the angel of Exod 23:20-21 ('Behold, I am sending an angel before you ... my Name is in him') with Metatron, with usage-rights restricted to Moses alone. This is the central activation-site for the two-powers-in-heaven controversy (b. Sanhedrin 38a-b; b. Hagigah 15a; see central entry two-powers-in-heaven-...): the Metatron 'in whom is my Name' brings the figure close to a 'lesser-YHWH' status that the rabbinic-polemical category guards against. Maimonides condemned this reading as Christianising. 'Shem the Great' (Šēm hag-gādôl) is rendered as the proper name 'Shem son of Noah' per Cohen 1985 (the alternative 'the Great Name'/Tetragrammaton-tradition is Schäfer's reading; the dispute is preserved). Lens-discipline disavowal: no Christian-Trinitarian pre-resolution of the two-powers controversy.

59
And the angels who are with him come and circle before the throne of glory — they on one side, and the living creatures on one side, and the Shekhinah upon the throne of glory in the middle. And one living creature ascends above the seraphim and descends upon the tabernacle of the youth, and says with a great voice, a still small voice: this is the throne of glory.
וּמַלְאָכִים Ū-malʾāḵīm אֲשֶׁר ʾăšer עִמּוֹ ʿimmō בָּאִים bāʾīm וְסוֹבְבִים wĕ-sōḇĕḇīm לִפְנֵי lip̄nē כִּסֵּא kissēʾ הַכָּבוֹד. hak-kāḇōḏ. הֵן Hen מִצַּד mi-ṣaḏ אֶחָד ʾeḥāḏ וְחַיּוֹת wĕ-ḥayyōt מִצַּד mi-ṣaḏ אֶחָד ʾeḥāḏ וּשְׁכִינָה ū-šĕḵīnâ עַל ʿal כִּסֵּא kissēʾ הַכָּבוֹד hak-kāḇōḏ בָּאֶמְצַע. bā-ʾemṣaʿ. וְחַיָּה Wĕ-ḥayyâ אַחַת ʾaḥaṯ עוֹלָה ʿōlâ עַל ʿal הַשְּׂרָפִים haś-śĕrāp̄īm וְיוֹרֶדֶת wĕ-yōreḏeṯ עַל ʿal מִשְׁכַּן miškan הַנַּעַר han-naʿar וְאוֹמֶרֶת wĕ-ʾōmereṯ בְּקוֹל bĕ-qōl גָּדוֹל gāḏōl קוֹל qōl דְּמָמָה dĕmāmâ דַקָּה: ḏaqqâ: זֶה zeh כִּסֵּא kissēʾ הַכָּבוֹד. hak-kāḇōḏ.
Notes Verse 59

Shekhinah on the throne (identified with the §§3-39 cosmic-body Creator-figure); ḥayyot and angels arranged. 'Tabernacle of the youth' (miškan han-naʿar) is Metatron's distinct dwelling. 'A great voice, a still small voice' (qôl gādôl, qôl dĕmāmâ daqqâ) — the famous 1 Kgs 19:12 oxymoron transposed into the Hekhalot throne-room cosmography.

60
Immediately the ofannim grew silent, the angels were still, the bands of watchers and holy ones [Aramaic: ʿirin we-qaddishin] hushed and ⟨…⟩ to the river of fire. And the living creatures set their faces to the land. And this youth brings the silent fire and places it in the ears of the living creatures, so that they shall not hear the voice of the speech of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Explicit Name which the youth mentions at that moment.
מִיָּד Miy-yāḏ שָׁתְקוּ šāṯĕqū הָאוֹפַנִּים, hā-ʾōp̄annīm, דָּמְמוּ dāmmĕmū הַמַּלְאָכִים, ham-malʾāḵīm, גְּדוּדִין gĕḏūḏīn עִירִין ʿīrīn וְקַדִּישִׁין wĕ-qaddīšīn חָשׁוּ ḥāšū וְרָ‹...›ן wĕ-rā‹...›n לִנְהַר li-nĕhar דִּינוּר. dīnūr. וְחַיּוֹת Wĕ-ḥayyōt נוֹתְנוֹת nōtĕnōt אֶת ʾeṯ פְּנֵיהֶם pĕnēhem לָאָרֶץ. lā-ʾāreṣ. וְהַנַּעַר Wĕ-han-naʿar הַזֶּה haz-zeh מֵבִיא mēḇīʾ אֶת ʾeṯ הָאֵשׁ hā-ʾēš הַחֲרִישִׁית ha-ḥărīšīt וְנוֹתֵן wĕ-nōtēn בְּאָזְנֵיהֶם bĕ-ʾoznēhem שֶׁל šel חַיּוֹת ḥayyōt כְּדֵי kĕ-ḏē שֶׁלֹּא še-lōʾ יִשְׁמְעוּ yišmĕʿū אֶת ʾeṯ קוֹל qōl הַדִּיבּוּר had-dibbūr שֶׁל šel הַקָּדוֹשׁ־בָּרוּךְ־הוּא hak-qādōš-bārūḵ-hūʾ וְאֶת wĕ-ʾeṯ שֵׁם Šēm הַמְפֹרָשׁ ham-mĕp̄ōrāš שֶׁהַנַּעַר še-han-naʿar מַזְכִּיר mazkīr בְּאוֹתָהּ bĕ-ʾōtâ שָׁעָה. šāʿâ.
Notes Verse 60

The theurgical core — the cosmic silence imposed on the throne-room so that the lesser angelic ranks (ofannim, angels, watchers-and-holy-ones, ḥayyot) do not hear the Shem ha-Mephorash (Explicit Name) which Metatron-the-youth pronounces. The 'silent fire' (hā-ʾēš ha-ḥărîšît) is the theurgical-protective apparatus. Aramaic ʿîrîn wĕ-qaddîšîn 'watchers and holy ones' (Dan 4:14). Cross-corpus: 1 Kgs 19:12 (the still small voice); Hab 2:20; Zech 2:17; Rev 8:1 'there was silence in heaven for about half an hour' — Cohen 1985 notes Rev 8:1 as the closest cross-corpus match. Maimonides condemned the entire pronounceable-Tetragrammaton tradition (Mishneh Torah, Yesodei ha-Torah 6:2). Lens-discipline disavowals: (i) no Christian-Apocalyptic Rev 8:1 pre-resolution; (ii) no Sitchin/engineered-communication-protocol pre-resolution; the cosmic-silence is a theurgical-mystical convention in the religious-mystical register.

61
And thus he calls upon the Holy One, blessed be He, by his name — the pure, the clean, the holy, the mighty, the strong, the powerful, the beloved, the valiant, the honored, and the awesome, mighty: YHW AHARVI HA-ḤAYYE YHWH EHYEH-ASHER-EHYEH HA-ḤAY YHWH YOAY HAVAH HH WH ⟨…⟩ HY HH HH YHY HY HY HY HWH. Living One of the worlds. This is his name forever, and this is his memorial for generation upon generation. And blessed is the name of the glory of his kingdom forever and ever.
וְכָךְ Wĕ-ḵāḵ הוּא hūʾ קוֹרֵא qōrēʾ אוֹתוֹ ʾōṯō לְקָדוֹשׁ־בָּרוּךְ־הוּא lĕ-qādōš-bārūḵ-hūʾ בִּשְׁמוֹ bi-šĕmō הַזַּךְ haz-zaḵ הַטָּהוֹר haṭ-ṭāhōr וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ wĕ-hak-qādōš וְהָאַדִּיר wĕ-hā-ʾaddīr וְהֶחָזָק wĕ-he-ḥāzāq וְהָעִזּוּז wĕ-hā-ʿizzūz וְהָאָהוּב wĕ-hā-ʾāhūḇ וְהַגִּבּוֹר wĕ-hag-gibbōr וְהַנִּכְבָּד wĕ-han-niḵbāḏ וְהַנּוֹרָא wĕ-han-nōrāʾ אַדִּיר: ʾaddīr: יְהוֹ YHW אַהֲרְבִי ʾaharbī הַחַיֵּי ha-ḥayyē יְהוָה YHWH אֶהְיֶה־אֲשֶׁר־אֶהְיֶה ʾehyeh-ʾăšer-ʾehyeh הַחַי ha-ḥay יְהוָה YHWH יוֹאַי Yōʾay הָבָה Hāḇâ הה hh וה wh ‹...› ‹...› הי hy הה hh הה hh יהי yhy הי hy הי hy הי hy הוה. hwh. חַי Ḥay הָעוֹלָמִים. hā-ʿōlāmīm. זֶה Zeh שְׁמוֹ šĕmō לְעוֹלָם lĕ-ʿōlām וְזֶה wĕ-zeh זִכְרוֹ ziḵrō לְדֹר lĕ-ḏōr דֹר. dōr. וּבָרוּךְ Ū-ḇārūḵ שֵׁם šēm כְּבוֹד kĕḇōd מַלְכוּתוֹ malḵūtō לְעוֹלָם lĕ-ʿōlām וָעֶד. wā-ʿed.
Notes Verse 61

The Ineffable Name as Metatron pronounces it — 11-fold divine-attribute list followed by a magical-name string including YHW + ʾEhyeh-ʾašer-ʾEhyeh (Exod 3:14) + YHWH + 'Living One of the worlds' (ḥay hā-ʿôlāmîm, Dan 12:7). Scriptural anchor Exod 3:15 ('this is my name forever, and this is my memorial for generation upon generation'). The recitation enacts the daily Shemaʿ / Amidah divine-name liturgy in mystical-magical form.

62
And its interpretation in the tongue of purity: YEHI HAHIW HAYAH HI WOT HU YAH HOHI YEHAH YIHAH YU YEHU HAHI WEHI HAH YIHYEH ⟨…⟩H HAH YEHI HU YAH ⟨…⟩H HI HAH YEHU YU ḤAY HI HOH. Blessed is the name of the glory of his kingdom forever and ever.
וּפֵרוּשׁוֹ Ū-pērūšō בִּלְשׁוֹן bi-lšōn טָהֳרָה: ṭohŏrâ: יְהִי yĕhī הָהִיו hāhīw הָיָה hāyâ הִי hī וֹת wōt הוּ hū יָהּ yāh הוֹהִי hōhī יְהָה yĕhâ יִיהָ yīhâ יוּ yū יְהוּ yĕhū הָהִי hāhī וְהִי wĕhī הָה hāh יִהְיֶה yihyeh ‹...›ה ‹...›h הָה hāh יְהִי yĕhī הוּ hū יָה yāh ‹...›ה ‹...›h הִי hī הָה hāh יְהוּ yĕhū יוּ yū חַי ḥay הִי hī הוֹה. hōh. בָּרוּךְ Bārūḵ שֵׁם šēm כְּבוֹד kĕḇōd מַלְכוּתוֹ malḵūtō לְעוֹלָם lĕ-ʿōlām וָעֶד. wā-ʿed.
Notes Verse 62

The letter-permutation method: 'pure-language interpretation' = continuous YHWH-letter permutations (Y/H/W combinations). Anticipates Abraham Abulafia's prophetic-Kabbalah by centuries (Scholem 1965). The breathing-meditation register is the pĕrûš bi-lšôn ṭohŏrâ 'interpretation in the tongue of purity' convention.

63
Shi'ur Qomah. Chapter 3.
שִׁעוּר Šiʿūr קוֹמָה. Qōmâ. פ P[ereq] ג G[immel]
Notes Verse 63

Structural heading: Perek Gimmel 'Chapter 3', the alphabetic-acrostic hymn appended to the body-measurement core. Functions as the liturgical-closing companion piece.

64
God, by your word, our Lord — Righteousness, host of Israel, those who hope for your righteousness; in you they are justified, Selah. Your righteousnesses they shall exalt, to exalt you together they shall open the mouth, answer, and say: 'YHWH our Lord, how majestic is your name' [Ps 8:2].
אֵל ʾēl בְּמַאֲמָרְךָ bĕ-maʾămārĕḵā אֲדוֹנֵינוּ ʾăḏōnēnū צֶדֶק Ṣedeq צְבָא ṣĕḇāʾ יִשְׂרָאֵל Yiśrāʾēl מְיַחֲלֵי mĕyaḥălē צִדְקֶךָ. ṣiḏqeḵā. בְּךָ Bĕ-ḵā יַצְדִּיקוּ yaṣdīqū סֶלָה. selâ. צִדְקוֹתֶיךָ Ṣiḏqōteḵā יְרוֹמְמוּ yĕrōmĕmū לְרוֹמֵם lĕ-rōmēm לְךָ lĕ-ḵā יַחַד yaḥaḏ יִפְצְחוּ yip̄ṣĕḥū פֶּה peh יַעֲנוּ yaʿănū וְיֹאמְרוּ: wĕ-yōʾmĕrū: «יְהוָה 'YHWH אֲדוֹנֵינוּ ʾăḏōnēnū מָה mâ אַדִּיר ʾaddīr שִׁמְךָ». šimḵā.'
Notes Verse 64

Opening of the alphabetic-acrostic hymn. Scriptural anchor Ps 8:2 ('YHWH our Lord, how majestic is your Name'). The Hebrew אֲדוֹנֵינוּ is rendered 'our Lord' per standard Anglophone Jewish-studies convention.

65
You are mighty and your Name is mighty. You are strong and your Name is strong. You are valiant and your Name is valiant. You are blessed and your Name is blessed. You are pure and your Name is pure. You are great and your Name is great. You are powerful and your Name is powerful. You are exalted and your Name is exalted ⟨…⟩.
אַתָּה ʾattâ אַדִּיר ʾaddīr וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā אַדִּיר. ʾaddīr. אַתָּה ʾattâ אַמִּיץ ʾammīṣ וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā אַמִּיץ. ʾammīṣ. אַתָּה ʾattâ אַבִּיר ʾabbīr וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā אַבִּיר. ʾabbīr. אַתָּה ʾattâ בָּרוּךְ bārūḵ וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā בָּרוּךְ. bārūḵ. אַתָּה ʾattâ בָּרוּר bārūr וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā בָּרוּר. bārūr. אַתָּה ʾattâ גָּדוֹל gāḏōl וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā גָּדוֹל. gāḏōl. אַתָּה ʾattâ גִּבּוֹר gibbōr וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā גִּבּוֹר. gibbōr. אַתָּה ʾattâ גֵּאֶה gēʾeh וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā גֵּאֶה gēʾeh ‹...›. ‹...›.
Notes Verse 65

Acrostic hymn — 'You are X and your Name is X.' The triple-name liturgical pattern is late-antique piyyut form. Each epithet is paired with itself as divine-Name: divine-attribute = divine-Name (the šēm wĕ-ṣiwwâh identity formula). Many epithets have multiple valid English equivalents; the translation uses standard scholarly conventions while preserving the structural triplet.

66
You are distinguished and your Name is distinguished. You are judge and your Name is judge. You are majesty and your Name is majesty and splendor. You are splendid and your Name is splendid. You are enduring and your Name is enduring. You are appointed and your Name is appointed. You are pure and your Name is pure. You are mighty and your Name is mighty. You are gracious and your Name is gracious. You are Ḥ⟨…⟩. You are clean and your Name is clean. You are unique and your Name is unique.
אַתָּה ʾattâ דָּגוּל dāḡūl וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā דָּגוּל. dāḡūl. אַתָּה ʾattâ דַּיָּן dayyān וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā דַּיָּן. dayyān. אַתָּה ʾattâ הוֹד hōḏ וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā הוֹד hōḏ וְהָדָר. wĕ-hāḏār. אַתָּה ʾattâ הָדוּר hāḏūr וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā הָדוּר. hāḏūr. אַתָּה ʾattâ וָתִיק wātīq וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā וָתִיק. wātīq. אַתָּה ʾattâ וָעֵד wāʿēḏ וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā וָעֵד. wāʿēḏ. אַתָּה ʾattâ זַךְ zaḵ וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā זַךְ. zaḵ. אַתָּה ʾattâ חָסִין ḥāsīn וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā חָסִין. ḥāsīn. אַתָּה ʾattâ חַנּוּן ḥannūn וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā חַנּוּן. ḥannūn. אַתָּה ʾattâ ח‹...›. ḥ‹...›. אַתָּה ʾattâ טָהוֹר ṭāhōr וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā טָהוֹר. ṭāhōr. אַתָּה ʾattâ יָחִיד yāḥīḏ וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā יָחִיד. yāḥīḏ.
Notes Verse 66

Acrostic continuation through letters dalet-yod. yāḥîd ('unique/only') at letter yod is theologically loaded (cf. Shemaʿ's YHWH ʾeḥād 'YHWH is one'). The English collisions (zaḵ='pure' / ṭāhôr='pure'-or-'clean') are unavoidable in the acrostic-typology constraints.

67
You are mighty and your Name is mighty. You are ablaze and your Name is ablaze. You are ⟨…⟩. You are awesome and your Name is awesome. You are feared and your Name is feared. You are long-suffering and your Name is long-suffering. You are strong and your Name is strong. You are redeemer and your Name is redeemer. You are righteous and your Name is righteous. You are pure and your Name is pure. You are holy and your Name is holy. You are merciful and your Name is merciful. You are Shadday and your Name is Shadday. You are perfect and your Name is perfect. ⟨…⟩ blessed ⟨…⟩.

Šadday. אַתָּה ʾattâ תָּמִים tāmīm וְשִׁמְךָ wĕ-šimḵā תָּמִים. tāmīm. ‹...› ‹...› בָּרוּךְ bārūḵ ‹...›. ‹...›.
Notes Verse 67

Acrostic completion through letter taw. Šadday preserved untranslated per Hebrew-Bible-glossary convention (the canonical divine name). The closing bārûḵ doxology anchors the entire chapter back into the standard berakhah-formula.

Contents

    Wheel of Heaven is an open, multilingual reading of the ancient world's creation traditions — Raëlian, biblical, Mesopotamian, and others — through a single working hypothesis: that the beings called Elohim were a small advanced human civilization that came here, designed life on Earth, and left a record in the religious texts. The reading runs across twelve ages of the precessional cycle, from the project's beginning twenty-two thousand years ago to the present age of disclosure and into the long future the next Great Year is opening. The site is free, source-aware, and built so the work can be checked.
